title: Mammography AI malignancy score associated with long-term breast cancer risk
summary: In 2,412 women with invasive breast cancer and 4,995 matched controls from two US cohorts, a one-unit increase in a commercial AI malignancy score on mammograms taken 2-5.5 years before diagnosis carried 20% greater odds of invasive cancer (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.17-1.22; AUC 0.63). Odds were similar for interval (OR 1.20) and advanced cancers (OR 1.23). The AI score was applied rather than developed here, discrimination was modest, and the abstract reports its contribution beyond density measures.
ai_technology: Commercial AI mammography malignancy score (1-10) used as a long-term risk marker

evidence.tested: Matched case-control comparison in two US mammography cohorts using conditional logistic regression, likelihood ratio tests and bootstrapping.
evidence.unknown: Prospective risk-stratification value, how much the AI score adds beyond density measures, and generalization to other AI systems; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Provides the AI malignancy score whose association with later invasive, interval and advanced cancer is measured.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
